Each entry records why. Add to this file only when you can name the amendment that replaced the line.

_reason_groups.superseded_by: the v936.2 / v936.3 / v936.4 / v936.4a amendments in this checkout (code commits 46f2209, 759702a, 88ecc45, e33f2bc; 2026-08-21/22)
_reason_groups.why: 32 lines that describe a funnel and a report shape the code no longer produces. Measured over 119 nodes / 495 variants (docs/experiments/v936-judge-backtest-2026-08-21/), the old rule failed the variant the operator actually chose 44.5% of the time, because parse_judge_reply computed `verdict = fail if (compliance or text_errors or MODEL_SAID_FAIL)` and the model's free-form word could hard-fail a wardrobe difference. v936.4 makes the verdict STRUCTURAL — fail iff one of five named hard lists is non-empty (compliance, text_errors, and the new identity_errors / hero_action_errors / corruption_errors), with element_misses / artifacts / text_notes / reasons demoted to warnings and the model's word kept as `model_verdict` telemetry. v936.2 split rendered text into failing `text_errors` and inert `text_notes` after the blanket rule recommended nothing on 13 of 13 nodes. v936.3 added the continuity stage (face_sim + color_distance against the chain parent's operator-APPROVED frame), two ranking axes, `continuity_anchor`, per-variant `continuity` and the recommendable `continuity` confidence. v936.4 also renamed `confirmed` to `repeat_stable` and REMOVED it from CONF_RECOMMENDABLE (4/8 operator agreement; a second read by the same model measures repeatability, not correctness), so the agreement buckets and the graduation denominator both had to be re-cut, and added report-level `systemic_miss`. Keeping the old lines would have canon name a `confirmed` state the code no longer produces and a five-field judge dict that is now nine. Rule coverage unchanged: v936 is still one section with one `## ` heading (the new sub-headings are prose-first so they mint no phantom rule), and check_rule_index.py stays PASS.

The read-caption overlay CLAIMS a high age and the picture is SUPPOSED to look younger than the claim — that gap is the hook (control overlay 'I'M 74 ... I do daily to move like I'm 35'; amplifier 'my biological age is 41.3'; mentor's 'move like I'm 35'; the model account @agelessjudy; momohsen64 at 62 reading forty). So 'drifting younger' was never a defect to prevent. The peer review then caught that the replacement claim ('the drift that matters is identity') was ALSO unproven at n=1. The clause now separates PROVEN (wardrobe, footwear, room, light carry), UNPROVEN (face/identity fidelity, eye-checked against the avatar every time) and NOT A TARGET (apparent age). Rule coverage unchanged: v950 is still one section with one heading, and check_rule_index.py stays PASS.
